steps.say: Probability is a number from 0 to 1. 0 means it cannot happen, 1 means it is certain, and 0.5 means even chance.
Two events that cannot happen at the same time are mutually exclusive. When you roll one die you cannot get a 2 and a 5 at once.
Two events can happen at the same time if they can both be true. Rolling an even number and rolling a number greater than 3 can both be true when you roll a 6.
The probabilities of all the possible outcomes add up to 1. If the chance of rain is 0.35, the chance of no rain is 1 − 0.35 = 0.65.
To estimate a probability, do an experiment many times. The probability is about the number of times it happened divided by the number of trials. More trials give a better estimate.

check.prompt: The probability of rain tomorrow is 0.3. What is the probability that it does not rain? Give a decimal.
You roll one die. Which two events cannot happen at the same time?

options.text: rolling an even number and rolling a 6
options.why: A 6 is even, so both can happen.

options.text: rolling a number less than 4 and rolling a 3
options.why: A 3 is less than 4, so both can happen.

hints: One roll gives only one number.
Check if any number fits both events.
check.explanation: You cannot roll a 2 and a 5 on a single roll, so these cannot happen together.
